blocks.text: To reabsorb water from the loop of Henle and the collecting duct, nephrons create and keep a high concentration of salt (NaCl) in the fluid around them. This is done by the counter-current mechanism.

items: The descending limb is permeable to water but not to salts. As filtrate flows down it, water leaves by osmosis into the salty fluid outside.
The ascending limb is impermeable to water but actively transports sodium ions out of the filtrate; chloride ions follow. This keeps the salt concentration of the surrounding fluid high.
As urine passes down the collecting duct through this salty fluid, water moves out by osmosis and enters the blood through the vasa recta.

blocks.alt: Left: a nephron with numbered steps: 1 filtration from the glomerulus into the capsule under high pressure; 2 reabsorption, mostly in the proximal tubule, of glucose, amino acids, salts and about 75% of the water; 3 secretion into the distal tubule of H+, NH4+, K+ and drugs. The medulla is shaded saltier with depth; water leaves the descending limb, Na+ is pumped out of the ascending limb, and water leaves the collecting duct. Right: flow charts for ADH and aldosterone.
blocks.caption: The counter-current mechanism: the medulla gets saltier with depth (original diagram after topic 14.2.1).
blocks.long_description: Urine forms in three steps. Filtration: the efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent, so glomerular pressure stays high and pushes water, urea, glucose, amino acids, vitamins and salts into Bowman's capsule, about a fifth of the plasma, while proteins and cells stay in the blood. Reabsorption: most useful material returns in the proximal tubule; the descending limb lets water out, the ascending limb pumps salt out, and the distal tubule and collecting duct take back more. Secretion: the distal tubule adds H+, NH4+, K+ and drugs. The salty medulla made by the loop draws water out of the collecting duct, more when ADH makes the duct permeable; aldosterone makes the distal tubule and duct take back Na+, and water follows.
